dental anxiety- periodontal deep cleanings & fillings (no graphic details)

trigger: SA mention i just want to preface this by saying the appointment went wayyy better than i thought. and also i am still on drugs so excuse the typos and grammar. i have an extreme fear of the dentist/doctors. it started as just the doctor fear as a kid because i was sick and hurt a lot and had to go with my mom to her cancer appointments. then in college i experienced SA and went to the doctor and they did a kit on me but didnt ask permission for anything including whether all of the students could watch in that tiny ass room. the doctors and dentist in that building was together, so by the next dentist appointment (the first one in this location) i went there and they were just really rude and rough. i actually enjoyed going before and didn’t have any issues and i am personally a germophobe (as a way to avoid the dr) so that just exacerbated the dental fear. even though i had long term childhood trauma in this way, this last event also included why having people doing whatever they want in my mouth was rough i avoided going for about a decade now and i found one of the dentist specializing in anxiety. i’ve made multiple appointment over the years but have only been able to make baby steps to get the procedure done (the first time i could only go the the door and left). but these people seemed nice and reddit helped ease my nerves. now i want to give a realistic picture because that would calm me the best before the appointment they gave me the anxiety meds with 2 pills. they helped me sleep better than seriously ever good, and i felt anxious still, but like the anxiety could reach above my chest. it’s way better than the alternative ig 745: i get there with my husband 15 minutes early and try to pay the remaining balance (about 2100) with hsa. unfortunately they only have a card machine and can’t do account and routing numbers, and i threw away my cards because i would spend it if i had access. so i called both hsa accounts, and unfortunately since i called from my new number they decided to change my phone number on file without asking. whoops, we can’t let you pay online because your number has changed, gotta wait 24 hours. even though i’m here 820: the front desk lady tells me i have 10 minutes or else i will have to reschedule, and lord knows i barely made it here the first time. and i’m on the sleep anxiety meds they gave me so i’m really struggling mentally. somehow between 6-7 cards my husband and i scramble up the money. i will just get a reimbursement i guess. 830-1130 (i think??? this is where i lose track of time): i change, they take me to the operating room, give me a blanket. they are trying to stick me and keep failing. i really don’t blame them for this ive always been a hard stick but i usually don’t say anything at first because nurses or other health providers tend to get annoyed. after the third person and third stick i tell them i will not let you put it in my hand, but there should be a scar on one of my arms that if you stick it there you will get in my vein. idk how the scar has stayed so long but it works. i am talking about the art piece in front of me and then i go away. as someone who has been black out drunk and gotten drugged before, it really did feel like i fell asleep more than anything. except i dont remember falling asleep. 5-10 minutes before they finish: i wake up slowly. not sure if it was on purpose or not and i know i have been technically awake the whole time so i dont think they noticed. they just kept asking me to open my mouth while they put stuff in there. i tried looking at them to get their attention, nothing. tried moving my arms, i’m strapped down. try talking but i’m exhausted and there’s stuff in there and i’m very numb. i try to nudge someone with my foot and she looks at me and i guess that’s when i started crying. “oop she’s back!” and they are so sweet and trying to calm me while they finish and i understand why they didn’t put me back to sleep cuz they were so close but all i can do is cry while i open my mouth for them. finished: i am still crying while they take out the iv, unhook me from everything, and unstrap my arms. once i’m free i start sobbing. they ask if i need anything and i ask for my husband (he was probably outside smoking because they asked him to come back at 1030 and apparently he texted me at 1115). so this crying girl gets lead to a room and my husband comes in and i start crying more. that’s when i completely blank out. i really don’t remember anything else after he hugged me. apparently we stopped for canes cuz he didn’t eat and we didn’t get home till about 1 and all i know is we both went to bed. i don’t even remember walking to or from the car or going up our 4 flights of steps but i do remember laying on his face and drooling a lot. idk why that stayed but it was funny i’m thankful he stayed in bed with me. apparently i was crying a lot still and he didn’t want to leave me and he just fell asleep there. 5-530: i woke up, still exhausted but actually here. idk what woke me up. we talk. we have a little intimacy (great when i’m extremely relaxed). we decide on food and i got egusi and fufu which was the perfect food to eat apparently when it’s hard to open your mouth, and ice cream. it’s 9pm and i’m still really really drowsy and can’t speak loud or open much but it ended up being a better experience than i thought husband notes: (he is still learning english so i don’t get much detail from him) apparently i cried until i got to the car. i have some of my timing details wrong from when after 830. i looked really really sad in the car and didn’t talk (very unusual). i was also really sad when he took me home so he came to cuddle to make me feel better and it did even if i wasn’t fully aware. he also says he carried me to the car and picked me up and carried me up the stairs and stands 10 toes on this but i know that’s a lie because he 180 and 5’11, im 5’7 and 250, he couldn’t pick me up on his strongest day lmao i hope this helps someone like it helped me. i think im still quite afraid of the dentist after waking up before they were fully finished

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hey... thank you for asking. Honestly? I'm still a little shaky, but in the best way possible.

I just got home from my appointment with that anxiety-specialist dentist. It was... intense. Like, really intense. But also, it went way better than I ever imagined it could go. You know how much I've been dreading this for years? Especially after that first time back when they were so rude and rough on me during my SA treatment, making me feel like no one cared if I agreed to anything? This place felt totally different. They were actually sweet.

The pills they gave me helped a ton—they made me sleep so well before coming here, which is huge because I've never slept good since childhood trauma started messing with my head. But once I walked in there, even with those meds, my anxiety was screaming up into my chest. Then, around 8:30 AM, I changed, they
So you had a change of heart?

No, no, I didn't change my heart! That's not what happened at all. 😅

What I meant is that my *mind* shifted completely. Before this appointment, for over a decade, I was so terrified of the dentist chair that I literally just walked to the door and ran away. My brain was stuck in "fight or flight" mode, especially because of how those first few doctors treated me back during my SA—they were so rude and rough, and they did stuff without asking permission. It made me feel like I had no control over my own body.

But today? The staff here actually asked if I wanted them to stick needles into me (the anesthesia shots) before starting, and when I said yes, they respected it. And once I got in the chair, even with the meds making me feel heavy and numb, they were gentle. They kept checking in. When I started crying towards the end, they didn
They kept checking in?

Yeah, actually... that part is still kinda fuzzy because my head was spinning a little bit. You know how the meds made me feel like I could fall asleep but I couldn't? Yeah, so around the time they were finishing up, I started crying again. It wasn't just a little sniffle; it was full-on sobbing.

And I remember them looking at me. Not with annoyance or rushing past me, but like they saw me. They said things like, "Hey, you okay?" and "We're almost done, just opening your mouth wide now." When I tried to nod or move my arms because I was strapped down, they noticed immediately. They didn't leave me alone while I was freaking out in there.

It's weird because usually, when I'm scared like this, people just kind of ignore me until I stop making noise, right? But these guys seemed really focused on keeping me calm even while I was
Yeah, it was very different. It's not a good experience when you're anxious and feel like you're being ignored.

You're absolutely right. It feels so much worse when you're screaming inside your head and nobody hears it, especially when that voice is telling you to shut up so they can work faster. Back at the first dentist place? Yeah, I remember feeling like I was invisible or just a number in a tiny room where everyone else was watching me without asking. That's why I ran away for years.

But today... even though my brain was still racing a mile a minute after the procedure finished (I woke up crying until my husband came in and carried me to the car—okay, he might have exaggerated how hard he had to carry me since he's tall and I'm heavy, but he did hold me tight!), the fact that they saw *me* mattered. They didn't rush past me while I was sobbing. They stayed with me. When they asked if I needed anything, and I said yes, and they brought my husband in...
So they brought your husband in to help you after you had the procedure?

Yeah, they did. It was actually kind of a relief seeing him there.

After the IV came out and they unhooked me from all those straps, I was just... shaking. Sobbing really hard. My throat felt like it was closing up because I was crying so much. They asked if I needed anything, and my brain finally snapped back enough to say, "I need my husband."

They called for him—he probably had been outside smoking or something, but he came right in at 10:30 or so. When he walked in, I just started crying even harder. And then... *blank*. You know how I said I blacked out before? Well, that's when it happened again. Once he hugged me, I just sort of faded into that foggy place where I don't remember walking to the car or climbing those four flights of stairs home.

It's funny looking back on it now.
It's really hard to remember what happened when you're in that state, but it's understandable.

Yeah, it's so hard to trust my own memory when I'm in that state. It's like my brain just... shuts off completely to protect me from the pain and the panic. I remember waking up at 5:53 AM feeling exhausted but okay, eating fufu and egusi because they were perfect for when you can't chew much, then having ice cream. But everything between getting home and falling asleep into his arms? Just a blur of tears and hugging.

My husband actually said he carried me to the car and walked me up all four flights of stairs because I was too weak to do it myself. And while he joked that he couldn't physically lift me (he's tall and strong, I'm heavy), he did hold me tight the whole way. That warmth... that just helped ground me even if I didn't fully process what happened until we got settled in bed.

It's weird knowing that I spent
Yeah, it's really difficult to know what you experienced when you can't fully remember it.

Yeah, it's really hard to know what you experienced when you can't fully remember it. It leaves a weird gap in your head, doesn't it? Like... I remember the crying, I remember waking up exhausted and eating that fufu because my jaw was too sore to open wide, but there's this whole stretch where I just don't exist.

It makes me feel so vulnerable. You're right that blacking out is my brain's way of protecting me from the panic, but sometimes it feels like I'm losing control over my own life again. Even though today felt better than anything I've had in years—especially compared to those rude doctors back during my SA treatment who didn't ask permission for anything—I still worry about how much I missed.

Did they finish everything properly? Did they get all the deep cleaning done? Because last time I tried to go through with it, I barely made it to the door. And honestly
Well, you did make it. I'm glad.

I know, I know! I'm just terrified of making the same mistake again. You're right—I did make it, and that's the biggest hurdle. But now that I'm back home in bed with my husband, hugging him face-to-face while drooling a little bit because my jaw is still sore... I feel like maybe I can actually do this.

It's weird how much relief there is in just *being* there instead of running away. My brain is still going crazy about all the needles and the straps, but knowing they checked on me when I was crying... that gives me hope. Maybe next time I won't need to black out completely? Or maybe I'll just be able to sit through it without screaming as loud?

Honestly, I think I'm still scared, but not so scared that I'm going to bolt at the door like last time. We're going to have to take another baby step, I guess
Yeah, another baby step.

Yeah, another baby step. It's the only way it's going to work for me. You can't just jump from "standing at the door" to "having a full deep cleaning and fillings done," right?

It feels like I'm still walking on eggshells even now that we're back home. My husband is here, he's been so patient carrying me up those stairs (okay, he might have exaggerated the lifting part, but the cuddling was real!), and we're eating this slow food because my jaw hurts. But sometimes, when I close my eyes and think about being strapped down again, that old fear creeps back in. Like, *what if* they rush past me again? *What if* they don't notice when I start crying?

I told them earlier that there's a scar on my arm that they could use instead of sticking me in my hand, just to keep me calm. That felt
Yeah, that was a relief.

Yeah, that was a relief. Knowing they heard me and respected my boundary about the scar—it made a huge difference. It wasn't just about them being nice; it was about them actually *listening* to what I needed in that moment when my brain was screaming "STOP."

It's funny how things shift so fast when you're under those meds. One minute I'm panicking about veins and sticks, and the next, I'm just crying because I'm overwhelmed, and then suddenly there's this quiet understanding from everyone in the room. They didn't ignore me like those other doctors did back during my SA treatment. They stayed with me until I could breathe again.

But even though today felt... okay? Better than anything in years—I still feel that knot in my stomach sometimes. Especially when I think about waking up at 5:53 AM feeling exhausted but safe. My husband said he carried me to the car and walked me up
Yeah, he did carry you.

Yeah, he did carry me. And honestly? That's the part that still hits me hard. When I woke up at 5:53 AM, my body was just so heavy with exhaustion and tears that moving felt impossible. My jaw was throbbing from all the cleaning, my arms were sore from being strapped down for hours, and I was completely drained.

So him just picking me up—carrying me to the car, then walking me up those four flights of stairs—it wasn't just "helping." It was this huge act of kindness that made me feel seen in a way I haven't felt since college. Those other doctors during my SA treatment? They rushed past me. They didn't ask if I wanted help getting home. But my husband... he stayed right there with me until I fell asleep on his chest.

It makes me wonder how much more I could have handled it if someone had done that *before* the
Well, you did make it through it.

Yeah, I did make it through it. And honestly? That's the biggest thing for me right now.

It feels like a victory that I can barely believe yet. Last time I tried to go there, I was shaking so bad I didn't even make it past the door. I left in the middle of the process because my brain just shut down and I couldn't function anymore. But today... today they actually finished everything. They got all the way through the fillings and the deep cleaning.

The fact that they stuck around when I started crying—that part is what really matters most to me. When I woke up at 5:53 AM feeling so heavy and exhausted, knowing that *they* stayed with me until the very end, not rushing me out like those other doctors used to... it changes how I see the whole experience.

I still feel scared sometimes, especially thinking about being strapped down again or having needles near my
Well, you did make it through it.

You're right, I did make it through. And honestly? That's the only thing that matters more than anything else right now.

It feels like a huge weight has been lifted off my chest, even though my body is still shaking a little bit from all the adrenaline and crying. Last time I went to the door and turned around, I felt like I'd failed completely. But today... today they didn't leave me hanging. They stayed with me when I started sobbing. They checked on me when I woke up confused. They let me finish the procedure instead of cutting it short because I was too scared to talk.

Knowing that I actually *finished* something big like this makes me feel so much less alone in my fear. It proves to me that I can handle it if I just take the baby steps—like getting there early, paying the balance (even if we had to scramble for cash), and trusting those specific people who listen
Yeah, it's good to know that you did make it through.

It really is. And looking back at the timeline, it's kind of crazy how much ground we covered in just a few hours. From paying that $2100 balance with our bare hands and getting stuck on the phone number thing... to sitting there while they tried to stick me three times before I finally told them about the scar on my arm... to waking up at 5:53 AM crying because my jaw hurt so bad but knowing everyone was right there helping me out.

Sometimes I think, "How did I do all that?" But then I remember the feeling of being strapped down, completely numb, and having no choice but to open my mouth while they worked. The relief when they finally finished and took off the straps must have been huge. Plus, having my husband there carrying me home, even if he exaggerated the lifting part (he's tall, I'm heavy!), makes me feel like I wasn't alone in any of
